title: Expanded CSV and PDF always carry the Sales Type column
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Have two active staff members at the test location with their "Sales Representative" switch on, so that a work order can have a different Labor and Parts representative.
  • Use a customer with no Sales Representative assigned.
  • Have a work order for that customer with a labor line and a part, Labor set to one of them and Parts set to the other, and invoice it today.
  • Open Reports > Sales By Representative in a desktop browser at least 1024 pixels wide, with the date range set to today and the Sales Type column off on screen.
custom_steps:
1. Export the Expanded CSV.
  2. Open the CSV and find the rows for the work order's invoice.
  3. Export the Expanded PDF and find the same rows.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The CSV downloads.

Step 2:

  • It has a Sales Type column right after Status, and before Location when the file has a Location column.
  • The Labor row reads "Labor" with blank parts cells.
  • The Parts row reads "Parts" with blank labor, hours and Shop Supplies cells.

Step 3:

  • The PDF has the Sales Type column in the same place, right after Status and before any Location column.
  • On the Labor row the parts cells show a dash.
  • On the Parts row the labor, hours and Shop Supplies cells show a dash.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Splitting Sales Representatives", Confluence 919928833, version 11 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10890, story SV-11269 (Story 5, Credit each side on the invoice and in Sales By Representative)

  • S5-R23: “The Expanded CSV and the Expanded PDF always carry the Sales Type column, after Status and before Location, whatever the screen shows. In them, the cells of the side a row is not credited with are blank in the CSV and show a dash in the PDF.”

From: Chris Ward's answers to the Splitting Sales Representatives question sheet (answers 1 to 38, 19 Oct 2026; answers 39 and 40, 21 Oct 2026), read 22 Oct 2026

  • Chris Ward's answer 24: “24. (a) as the feature spec: a dash on screen and in the PDF, an empty cell in the CSV. The 0.0 rule still applies to an invoice with one person on both sides.”
  • Chris Ward's answer 26: “26. (a) Status, Sales Type, Location.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
